title: Government Intervention Adventure 1: Taxes & Subsidies
welcome_lead: Today you'll levy a tax and pay a subsidy — and trace who really bears the cost.
meta_desc: Economics: direct vs indirect taxes, subsidies and tax incidence.
final_note: You compared direct and indirect taxes and explained subsidy incidence.

concepts.def: Govt payment to producer or consumer

walkthroughs.body_html:
Direct taxes hit income or wealth (income tax, corporation tax, capital gains).

Indirect taxes hit transactions (VAT, GST, excise duty).

Progressive: average rate ↑ with income (income tax). Regressive: ↓ (VAT). Proportional: flat rate.

A subsidy shifts supply right (producer) or demand right (consumer).

Pros: encourage merit goods (vaccines, education), protect jobs, support exports.

Cons: opportunity cost (tax revenue), can entrench inefficient firms, WTO restrictions on export subsidies.

Who pays a tax depends on relative elasticities.

If demand is more inelastic than supply, consumers bear more.

Cigarettes (inelastic demand) pass most of the duty onto smokers; luxury yachts (elastic demand) pass more onto sellers.

mcqs.q: When demand is more inelastic than supply, tax burden falls mostly on:

options: Growth is shown by the curve becoming straighter.
A tax set equal to the external cost of an activity — designed to internalise the externality so the private cost reflects the social cost. Used for pollution, congestion, sugary drinks.
A Pigouvian tax is a tax only on rich people.
A Pigouvian tax is a tax that funds government spending.

mcqs.q: How does the sign of cross elasticity of demand (XED) reveal product relationships?
options: Growth is shown by the curve becoming straighter.
The sign of XED doesn't matter — only the size does.
XED measures how often consumers cross-shop between stores.
Positive XED = substitutes (price of one rises, demand for the other rises); negative XED = complements (price of one rises, demand for the other falls); zero XED = unrelated goods.

mcqs.q: How is economic growth shown on a Production Possibility Curve?
options: Growth is shown by moving from inside the curve to a point on the curve.
XED measures how often consumers cross-shop between stores.
By an outward shift of the entire curve — reflecting an increase in productive capacity through more or better resources, technology, or skills.
Growth is shown by the curve becoming straighter.
